name: Link
role: The hero: a boy who lives among the Kokiri without a fairy of his own and becomes the Hero of Time.
appears: The whole adventure, as a child and as an adult.
note: He never speaks, beyond shouts and grunts. In the remake you cannot rename him, and there is one save file per console user.

name: Navi
role: Your fairy companion.
note: She helps you lock on (ZL) and gives advice. In the remake she only speaks when you call her with D-pad →, reads the Fairy Thoughts scattered around Hyrule and has a different dance for each song.

name: Princess Zelda
role: The princess of Hyrule, who dreams of the threat Ganondorf poses.
appears: Hyrule Castle (child), the Temple of Time and the ending.
note: She gives you Zelda's Letter and has Impa teach you Zelda's Lullaby. As she flees the castle she leaves you the Ocarina of Time and the Song of Time. Seven years later she returns with the Light Arrows and helps you against Ganon.

name: Ganondorf
role: King of the Gerudo and thief of the Triforce: the villain.
appears: Hyrule Castle (child), the Temple of Time and his castle.
note: The only male Gerudo, born once every hundred years. In the remake he appears as you open the way to the Sacred Realm with the Master Sword, freezes you and walks in to claim the Triforce.

name: Great Deku Tree
role: The guardian of Kokiri Forest.
note: He asks you to break the curse eating him from inside: his interior is the first dungeon. He gives you the Kokiri Emerald before he dies; in the remake his withered leaves rain over the whole forest. As an adult you meet his sprout.

name: Saria
role: Your best Kokiri friend and the Sage of Forest.
appears: Kokiri Forest, the Sacred Grove and the Forest Temple.
note: She gives you the Fairy Ocarina and teaches you Saria's Song: play it for hints. After Phantom Ganon she awakens as a Sage and gives you the Forest Medallion.

name: Mido
role: The self-proclaimed boss of the Kokiri.
note: He will not let you see the Great Deku Tree until you have a sword and shield. In the remake he means better than in the original.

name: Kaepora Gaebora
role: A wise owl who guides you.
note: He gives advice (you can ask him to repeat it) and flies you down from Death Mountain and Lake Hylia. In the remake he opens the Hall of Fallen Foes: after first reaching the adult era, go back to Kakariko Village as a child and talk to him. He also delivers your challenge trophies to your house.

name: Malon
role: Talon's daughter, from Lon Lon Ranch.
appears: Castle Town and Lon Lon Ranch.
note: She gives you the Weird Egg to wake her father and teaches you Epona's Song at the ranch.

name: Talon
role: The owner of Lon Lon Ranch.
appears: Hyrule Castle, Lon Lon Ranch and, as an adult, Kakariko Village.
note: He dozes off by the castle: wake him with the Wake-Up Cucco. His Super Cucco game gives a Bottle of Lon Lon Milk. As an adult, the Pocket Cucco wakes him.

name: Ingo
role: The Lon Lon Ranch hand.
note: As an adult he runs the ranch for Ganondorf. Beat him in the horse race to win Epona.

name: Epona
role: The ranch's mare and your horse.
appears: Lon Lon Ranch (child) and Hyrule Field (adult).
note: Win her in the race against Ingo and call her with Epona's Song. You need her for horseback archery and Big Poe hunting.

name: Impa
role: A Sheikah, Zelda's guardian and the Sage of Shadow.
appears: Hyrule Castle, Kakariko Village and the Shadow Temple.
note: She teaches you Zelda's Lullaby. After Bongo Bongo she awakens as a Sage and gives you the Shadow Medallion.

name: Darunia
role: Big Brother of the Gorons and the Sage of Fire.
appears: Goron City, Dodongo's Cavern and the Fire Temple.
note: Saria's Song gets him dancing and he gives you the Goron Bracelet; after King Dodongo, the Goron Ruby. After Volvagia he awakens as a Sage and gives you the Fire Medallion.

name: Princess Ruto
role: Zora princess and the Sage of Water.
appears: Zora Domain, Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly and the Water Temple.
note: You rescue her inside Lord Jabu-Jabu and she gives you the Zora Sapphire. As an adult she helps you in the Water Temple and, after Morpha, gives you the Water Medallion.

name: King Zora
role: King of the Zoras and Ruto's father.
note: As a child, show him Ruto's Letter to reach Zora Fountain. As an adult he is frozen: thaw him with Blue Fire and he gives you the Zora Tunic. In the trading sequence you hand him the Prescription.

name: Nabooru
role: The Gerudo second-in-command and the Sage of Spirit.
appears: Desert Colossus and the Spirit Temple.
note: As a child you promise to bring her the Silver Gauntlets. Twinrova controls her and she fights you as an Iron Knuckle. After Twinrova she gives you the Spirit Medallion.

name: Rauru
role: The Sage of Light.
appears: The Chamber of Sages, when you draw the Master Sword.
note: He explains what happened during the seven years you slept and gives you the Light Medallion.

name: Sheik
role: A mysterious Sheikah survivor.
appears: The Temple of Time and beside each adult temple.
note: Teaches you the Minuet of the Forest, Bolero of Fire, Serenade of Water, Nocturne of Shadow, Requiem of Spirit and Prelude of Light. In the remake Sheik carries a short sword. Sheik's identity is revealed after the Spirit Temple.

name: Koume and Kotake
role: Twin Gerudo witches, Ganondorf's foster mothers.
note: Koume wields fire and Kotake ice; together they merge into Twinrova.

name: Biggoron
role: A giant Goron at the summit of Death Mountain.
note: At the end of the adult trading sequence you bring him the Broken Goron Sword and the Specialty Eye Drops, and he forges the Biggoron Sword.

name: Medigoron
role: Biggoron's brother, a smith in Goron City.
note: In the base game he sells adult Link the Giant's Knife; open his shop with a bomb as a child (not yet confirmed for the remake).

name: Great Fairies
role: Six fairies in hidden fountains who grant magic and powers.
appears: Fountains behind walls or rocks all over Hyrule.
note: Play Zelda's Lullaby at their fountain. In the remake they ask for ever-larger Rupee offerings (one review says up to 500). They give the Magic Meter, Din's Fire, Farore's Wind, Nayru's Love and three gifts. Per Zelda Wiki, Din's Fire and the improved spin swapped fountains (not yet confirmed for the remake).

name: Business Scrub
role: A Deku Scrub who loves to sell.
appears: Grottos, dungeons and wherever you use a Business Scrub Seed.
note: Bounce its nut back with your shield so it gives up and offers you a deal. In the remake a Business Scrub Seed summons one wherever you are; one in Death Mountain Crater sells the Piece of Heart that used to be in the Ice Cavern, and one in Hyrule Field sells one for 100 Rupees and a password.

name: Happy Mask Salesman
role: The owner of the Happy Mask Shop in Castle Town.
note: He lends you masks to sell; pay him back and he lends you the next. In the end he lets you have the Mask of Truth (not yet confirmed for the remake).

name: Dampé
role: The Kakariko Graveyard gravekeeper.
note: As a child, his digging tour (faster in the remake, 10 Rupees a dig) can give you a Piece of Heart. As an adult, his ghost races you beneath the graveyard: the prize is the Hookshot.

name: Poe Collector
role: He buys Big Poe souls.
note: In the remake he gives you a Bottle for 5 Big Poes (it used to be 10), and a Gold Rupee for all 10.

name: Skull Kid
role: A mischievous child of the Lost Woods.
note: Play Saria's Song for him and he gives you a Piece of Heart; he also buys the Skull Mask. As an adult he attacks you.

name: Composer Brothers
role: Sharp and Flat, ghosts of the royal family's composers.
appears: The royal tomb in Kakariko Graveyard.
note: You learn the Sun's Song in their tomb. In the remake they have statues in the Hall of Fallen Foes, like your other rivals.

name: Cucco Lady
role: A Kakariko Village resident who raises Cuccos.
note: As a child, return her 7 Cuccos to the pen and she gives you a Bottle. As an adult she starts the trading sequence with the Pocket Egg and gives you Cojiro.

name: Castle Town Potion Shopkeeper
role: The owner of the Castle Town potion shop.
note: Sells potions. In the remake, help him with his errand and he gives you the fifth Bottle.

name: Guru-Guru
role: The musician in the Kakariko Village windmill.
note: As an adult he teaches you the Song of Storms. Playing it in the windmill as a child drains the well and opens the Bottom of the Well.

name: Bonooru and Pierre
role: Two scarecrows who love music.
note: Teach Bonooru eight notes as a child and play them to Pierre as an adult: that is the Scarecrow's Song.
